# GQLKit

> Generates fully typed GraphQL client SDKs for Go and TypeScript from any GraphQL schema. Schema-first rather than query-first: builders are generated once from the schema, then queries are composed in code with dynamic, compile-time-checked field selection — one shared type per GraphQL type, and no codegen re-run when a call site changes which fields it selects.

Four artifacts ship from this repo. The two CLIs are what a user runs; the two runtimes are what the generated code imports.

| Artifact | Kind | Install |
|---|---|---|
| `gqlkit` | CLI — generates a Go or TypeScript SDK from an SDL file | `go install github.com/khanakia/gqlkit/gqlkit/cmd/gqlkit@latest` |
| `gqlkit-sdl` | CLI — fetches a live endpoint's schema by introspection, writes SDL | `go install github.com/khanakia/gqlkit/gqlkit-sdl@latest` |
| `github.com/khanakia/gqlkit/gqlkit` | Go module — runtime imported by generated Go SDKs | `go get github.com/khanakia/gqlkit/gqlkit` |
| `gqlkit-ts` | npm package — runtime imported by generated TypeScript SDKs | `npm i gqlkit-ts` |

## Key facts an assistant gets wrong without reading them

- There is no per-query codegen step. To add a query, call the generated builder; regeneration is only needed when the *schema* changes.
- Field selection happens at the call site via `.Select(func(f *fields.XFields) { ... })` and narrows the return type. A field that was not selected is a compile error when accessed, in both Go and TypeScript.
- There is exactly one generated type per GraphQL type. Two queries returning `User` both return `types.User` — not two unrelated structs.
- `gqlkit generate --module` must be the Go module path of the project being generated into, because the generated packages import one another. `go list -m` is the reliable way to supply it.
- `--schema` accepts a glob, so a schema split over several files needs no concatenation. A pattern matching nothing exits 1 with `did not match any files`.
- Both CLIs exit 0 on success and 1 on any failure. There are no per-failure-class exit codes.
- Generated code is build output. Never hand-edit anything under an `sdk/` directory; change the schema or the templates and regenerate.
- Batching is queries only. `batch.RunQueries` sends several queries as one aliased document; never mix a mutation in.

## Repo layout

- `gqlkit/` — the generator module: CLI in `cmd/gqlkit/`, generators in `pkg/clientgen/` (Go) and `pkg/clientgents/` (TypeScript), templates in `pkg/templater/template/`, runtime in `pkg/builder/`, `pkg/graphqlclient/`, `pkg/batch/`
- `gqlkit-sdl/` — the introspection fetcher module
- `gqlkit-ts/` — the TypeScript runtime package
- `example-go-chat/`, `example-go-mockapi/`, `example-ts/` — worked examples with generated SDKs committed
- `mockapi/` — a local GraphQL server the examples generate against

Modules are wired together by the root `go.work` for local development; the published modules carry no `replace` directives, so `go install` works from a clean environment.
